final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead offered a narrower interpretation of the same evidence: that the rejection should be defended as a conservative unresolved-risk decision rather than as proof of a confirmed control failure. That reframing is more careful and removes an overbroad claim, but it does not resolve the core audit issue. Under the policy text, vendor rejection still must rest on admissible due-diligence evidence showing a material unresolved risk. On the record available to this role, the summarized evidence shows unresolved concerns and a follow-up condition, but it still does not clearly demonstrate that those concerns were formally or sufficiently material to meet the rejection standard rather than the follow-up or escalation standard. The distinction matters: narrowing an unsupported 'confirmed control failure' claim can make the rationale less overbroad, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats if the underlying materiality predicate for rejection remains unproven from admissible evidence alone.
